1.title: Quiz: Basics of Understanding Code
1.description: Testing understanding of how the computer executes commands, works with memory, and processes data.

questions.text: What happens in memory when `x = 5` is executed, then `x = 10`?
options: The old value 5 is erased, 10 is written
questions.explanation: Assignment overwrites the value.

questions.text:
What will this print?
```
a = 2
b = 3
a = b
b = a
output a, b
```
questions.explanation: a=b sets a=3. b=a sets b=3. Both 3.

questions.text:
What will this print?
```
output "2" + "2"
```
questions.explanation: Strings are concatenated.

questions.text:
What will this print?
```
output true AND false OR true
```
questions.explanation: true AND false = false. false OR true = true.

2.title: Quiz: Branching and Loops
2.description: Testing understanding of conditions, logical connectives, loops, and patterns.

questions.explanation: Two independent `if`. A and B are printed.

questions.text: What returns `NOT (true AND false)`?
questions.explanation: true AND false = false. NOT false = true.

questions.text: Which code correctly checks the range 1 to 10?
questions.explanation: Two complete conditions joined by AND.

questions.text: What is dangerous about the order `if x > 0 ... else if x > 10`?
options: For x=20 the first fires, the second is skipped
questions.explanation: Order cuts off options.

questions.text:
How many times will this run?
```
for i from 2 to 5:
    output i
```

3.title: Quiz: Arrays and Functions
3.description: Testing indexing, traversal, search, swap, and functions.

questions.text:
What will this print?
```
a = [10, 20, 30]
output a[1]
```
questions.explanation: Indexing from 0.

questions.text: What's wrong with starting the maximum search at `max = 0` for `[-5, -10]`?
options: The answer will be 0, although the numbers are negative
questions.explanation: 0 is greater than negatives.

questions.text: How to correctly swap a and b?
options: t = a; a = b; b = t
a = a + b; b = a - b; a = b - a
questions.explanation: Need a third variable.

questions.text: Where will an out-of-bounds error occur for `a = [1, 2, 3]`?
questions.explanation: Indices only 0, 1, 2.

questions.text:
What will this print?
```
function f(a):
    return a * 2
output f(3)
```
questions.explanation: Returns 6, outputs 6.

4.title: Quiz: Tracing and Complexity
4.description: Testing tracing, Big O, binary search, and selection sort.

questions.text: What is tracing?
options: Manually executing code with state recording
questions.explanation: You go line by line, writing down values.

questions.text: What does O(n) describe?
options: Growth of operations in the worst case as n grows
questions.explanation: About operations growth, worst case.

questions.text: How many checks maximum for 128 elements with binary search?
Why does binary search require a sorted array?
options: Discards half based on order — without sorting it may discard the right one
questions.explanation: Without order you may discard the half where the target is.

questions.text: What is selection sort's complexity?
questions.explanation: n times find minimum in O(n). Total O(n²).

5.title: Quiz: Recursion and Data Structures
5.description: Testing recursion, quicksort, hash tables, and graphs.

questions.text: What happens without a base case in recursion?
questions.explanation: Without a stop, calls accumulate to the limit, then error.

questions.text: What is quicksort's average complexity?
questions.explanation: Average — n log n. Worst — n².

questions.text: What is a collision in a hash table?
options: Two different keys give the same hash
questions.explanation: Different keys — one cell. Solved by a list.

questions.text: What does BFS use?
questions.explanation: Queue. Process first what we found earlier.

questions.text: Why `visited` in BFS?
options: So a vertex is not processed twice and no loop
questions.explanation: Without it you can go around a cycle forever.

6.title: Quiz: Advanced Algorithms
6.description: Testing greedy algorithms, DP, and the problem-solving approach.

questions.text: Does greedy always give the optimum?
questions.explanation: Only if the task has the greedy choice property.

questions.text: When is DP applicable?
questions.explanation: Need optimal substructure + overlapping subproblems.

questions.text: What is fib complexity via DP?
questions.explanation: Each number — once. O(n). Without DP — exponential.

questions.text: Where to start solving a task?
questions.explanation: Understanding data is the base.

questions.text: Which of these are boundary cases for an array?
options: Empty, one element, all same, maximum
questions.explanation: Everything on range boundaries.
